title: Investigate ingest backpressure oddity — scratch
content:
Summary:
Quick brain dump while investigating an odd behavior where traces and metrics drop for ~30s every ~10m, only for certain customers. Pattern seems correlated with a consumer-side backpressure incident but consumer lag metrics show near-zero. Objective is to reproduce, collect minimal repro commands, and hypotheses to hand off to SRE/infra.

Timeline & observed signal:
- 2024-11-01 10:02 UTC: first alert (monitoring) — latency SLO breach for trace-collection route /v1/spans for tenant=acme-inc; ephemeral; resolved automatically after ~32s. No deployments at that time.
- Subsequent alerts at ~10:12, 10:22, 10:32 — periodic ~10m cadence for ~3 hours, then stopped.
- Dashboards: span ingest rate drops 20–40% during window; error rate increases on ingress (503 / upstream timeout). Upstream logs show "Hook processing timeout: 30s exceeded" in several pods.
- Consumer lag (kafka topic obs.spans) reported as <10 messages for group obs-ingest-consumer; broker-end offsets are advancing.

Commands I ran (notes + outputs summarized):
1) List pods & restart suspects:
$ kubectl -n obs get pods -l app=ingest-ingress -o wide\# confirmed 3 replicas, rolling restarts performed later

2) Check pod logs around event window (tail + grep):
$ kubectl -n obs logs ingest-ingress-1 --since=1h | grep -E "timeout|error|panic|Hook processing" -n
...
2024-11-01T10:02:11Z ERROR server request failed: Hook processing timeout: 30s exceeded (handler=hook-eval)
2024-11-01T10:02:12Z WARN span dropped: sampling decision absent for tenant acme-inc

3) Kafka consumer group detail (consumer CLI):
$ kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-01:9092 --describe --group obs-ingest-consumer
GROUP           TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
obs-ingest-consumer obs.spans  0          123456          123460         4   consumer-1
...
Observation: lag small (0-5), yet spans disappearing at ingress.

4) Check proxy / envoy metrics for 5xx bursts:
- envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_5xx: brief spike coincident with timestamp. Upstream (ingest-worker) started returning 504 on a small subset of requests.

5) Query traces in Jaeger for sample tenant
- found many spans with parentId missing and trace incomplete (partial traces). Many have a top-level error tag: "ingest_failed: backpressure"

Error snippets repeated in logs:
- "Hook processing timeout: 30s exceeded"
- "proto: unexpected EOF while reading message" from grpc-read
- "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = backend queue full"
- "Dropped 12% of spans at ingress: sampling_rate override mismatch"

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Intermittent head-of-line blocking in hook evaluation workers. If one hook evaluation stalls (e.g., external enrichment call), ingress waits up to 30s (timeout) then marks request failed. But why consumer lag is low? Because failing requests are never enqueued to kafka (ingress returns 5xx before ack).
2) A recent change in hook chain ordering (PR #732) added an external HTTP enrichment to third-party, which is flaky under certain network paths (observed in traces where enrichment call to enrichment-service timed out).
3) Envoy connection pool exhaustion to upstream workers under bursty traffic. When exhausted, envoy returns 503/504 and ingress logs show hook timeouts. This would look like low consumer lag but higher client-side errors.
4) Misconfigured sampling override: some tenants had a per-tenant rule that triggers heavy synchronous enrichments for newly minted spans; this floods hook workers episodically (cron-like spikes).
5) GC / cgroup throttling on worker nodes causing pause >30s. Less likely because only some tenants affected and timing aligns to external service timeouts.

Repro steps to try (what I executed / plan to execute):
- Local repro: spin up minimal ingress + hook-eval that sleeps randomly (0–45s) to test timeout gating. Confirm that requests that hit >30s are failed and not enqueued to kafka.
- Canary: add extra logging (#message-id, hook durations) around hook-eval path to capture enrichment call latencies.
- Load test: run a synthetic traffic generator configured to hit tenants with heavy enrichments to reproduce head-of-line blocking and observe envoy upstream metrics.
- Temporarily revert PR #732 in canary and observe whether the 10m cadence disappears.

Quick diagnostics I left running:
- tcpdump on ingress pods capturing calls to enrichment-service: tcpdump -w /tmp/enrich.pcap host enrichment-service.namespace.svc.cluster.local and sample around next window.
- k8s cAdvisor scrapes for pod oom_kill / CPU throttling (set retention 24h).
- Jaeger query for traces with tag "ingest_failed" between 10:00–11:00 UTC.

Short-term mitigations to propose:
- Increase hook timeout from 30s -> 60s? (tradeoff: request holds resources longer; prevents immediate failure but can exacerbate head-of-line). Not first choice.
- Make enrichment call async: accept span, enqueue, enrich downstream. Requires schema & consumer coordination — medium effort.
- Rate-limit per-tenant sync enrichments at ingress (circuit-breaker): if a tenant triggers >X slow enrichments in Y window, skip enrichment and tag spans for deferred enrichment.
- Add a small threadpool isolation for hook-eval so one slow tenant doesn’t tie all workers.

Notes to self / gotchas:
- Do not confuse consumer lag (kafka) with ingress throughput. If ingress fails before enqueue, lag stays low.
- Check if sampling config rollout happened on 2024-10-31 — could explain tenant-specific rules.
- Check cloud provider egress NAT change (happened last week) that might affect enrichment-service path.

Next steps (action items):
- [ ] Add extra timing logs around enrichment HTTP calls (I will open quick PR with high-cardinality logs but gated behind debug flag) — assigned to me (Ravi).
- [ ] Coordinate with infra to keep tcpdump capture for 6 hours starting next observed window (cc: Diego).
- [ ] Re-run canary with PR #732 reverted on one canary nodepool (Arielle to assist).
- [ ] Add temporary rate limit / circuit-breaker at ingress for enrichment calls (proposal draft in OBS-4128).

Linked evidence / quick refs:
- Kibana query: k="ingest.request.path:/v1/spans AND log.level:ERROR AND message:"Hook processing timeout""
- Jaeger traces: tag ingest_failed=true (samples attached in OBS-4128 ticket)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-pipeline/pull/732 (suspect changes to hook chain)

Random notes (scratch):
- If enrichment-service is flaky under DNS TTL expiry, consider sticky DNS (clusterIP) or internal cache.
- Could also add a small per-tenant token bucket to limit synchronous enrichments to 10 req/s.
- Remember to redact tenant ids in support emails.

If I can't reproduce in 24h, escalate to infra on-call with full pod dumps and pcap (tagging Diego + Arielle).

-- end of dump (scratch)
